description: This line plot illustrates the relative change in performance across different transformer model layers when applying various key-value (KV) cache compression techniques, as compared to a baseline. The x-axis represents grouped model layers: “Layer1-4”, “Layer5-12”, “Layer13-20”, “Layer21-28”, and “Layer29-32”, indicating aggregated performance metrics over those layer ranges. The y-axis, labeled “Relative Change”, is scaled from -15% to +5% in linear increments of 5%, showing the percentage deviation from the baseline performance. Five distinct lines are plotted: the gray dashed line, labeled “Baseline of 4×tokens,4-bit”, remains flat at 0% across all layers, serving as the reference. The yellow line with circle markers, “LB-Avg of 1×tokens,16-bit”, starts near 0%, dips slightly to about -1% in Layer5-12, rises to ~0% in Layer13-20, dips again to -1% in Layer21-28, and ends near 0% in Layer29-32. The red line with square markers, “LB-Avg of 1×tokens,16-bit”, begins at 0%, drops to -2% in Layer5-12, stays flat at -2% through Layer13-20 and Layer21-28, then rises slightly to -1% in Layer29-32. The cyan line with circle markers, “RULER4k of 2×tokens,8-bit”, starts at 0%, declines to -3% in Layer5-12, further drops to -6% in Layer13-20, rises to -3% in Layer21-28, and ends near 0% in Layer29-32. The dark blue line with square markers, “RULER4k of 1×tokens,16-bit”, begins at 0%, drops sharply to -6% in Layer5-12, plummets to -15% in Layer13-20, recovers to -11% in Layer21-28, and ends at -2% in Layer29-32. The plot visually demonstrates how different compression configurations affect performance across model layers, with some methods showing significant degradation in middle layers before partial recovery in later layers.
